title: Chopin, Étude Op. 10 No. 5: Neeman and Cortot
work: Étude in G♭ major, Op. 10 No. 5
question: What part does the left hand play beneath the black-key runs in this étude?
intro: Chopin writes the right hand in fast figuration over the five black keys, with detached chords and octaves underneath. A loud phrase returns quietly. Cortot and Neeman play through to a final rapid passage in octaves.

recordings.label: Edward Neeman
recordings.note: Neeman’s Chopin recordings include the complete études and thirty-one mazurkas; he also plays piano duets with his wife, Stephanie.

recordings.label: Alfred Cortot, 1920
recordings.note: Cortot’s teaching edition treats this étude as a lesson in supple hand movement and a brilliant, finely connected touch.

passages.label: Opening: loud and quiet phrases
passages.note: The right-hand triplets run over detached left-hand chords; loud phrases are answered quickly and quietly.

passages.label: Extended phrase in D♭ major
passages.note: The triplets continue in D♭ major as the left hand extends the phrase beyond the four-bar groups of the opening.

passages.label: Return of the opening in G♭
passages.note: The opening figure returns in G♭ major, then grows quieter towards a passage marked very delicate and dying away.

passages.label: Arpeggios and closing octaves
passages.note: Wide arpeggios cover the keyboard before both hands finish in a fast, detached run of black-key octaves.
